correctness.rationale: For \(a=b+t(b+1)\), one has \(2^{a+1}\equiv1\pmod{2^{b+1}-1}\), hence \(\gcd(p,q)=1\). The explicit divisor box is therefore distinct and complement-stable; removing the two stated complementary pairs leaves exact sum \(2N_{b,t}\). The Mersenne factor \(2^{b+1}-1\) is not a nontrivial perfect power, and coprimality transfers its prime valuations unchanged to \(N_{b,t}\), excluding every nontrivial perfect-power representation. The logarithmic count follows from \(\log N_{b,t}=2(b+1)t\log2+O_b(1)\). The verifier independently checks a finite parameter rectangle but is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The paper's main two-parameter construction and its later primitive notion are natural objects to connect. The result does so uniformly for every fixed \(b\), without primality assumptions on the auxiliary factors, and gives the exact logarithmic scale of an explicit primitive subfamily. This is a structural refinement rather than a single numerical example; it also isolates the entire \(b=1\) row. Its value is not based on claiming the first infinite primitive family.
